statement: Find all positive integers \(w, x, y, z\) which satisfy \(w! = x! + y! + z!\).

For each \(r \in \mathbb{R}\), let \(T_r\) be the transformation of the plane that takes the point \((x, y)\) into the point \((2^r x,\; r \cdot 2^r x + 2^r y)\). Let \(F\) be the family of all such transformations (i.e.\ \(F = \{T_r : r \in \mathbb{R}\}\)). Find all curves \(y = f(x)\) whose graphs remain unchanged by every transformation in \(F\).
The area of a triangle is determined by the lengths of its sides. Is the volume of a tetrahedron determined by the areas of its faces?
Prove that for every prime number \(p\), there are infinitely many positive integers \(n\) such that \(p\) divides \(2^n - n\).

The geometric mean (G.M.) of \(k\) positive numbers \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k\) is defined to be the positive \(k\)-th root of their product. Show that the G.M.\ of a set \(S\) of \(n\) positive numbers is equal to the G.M.\ of the G.M.'s of all non-empty subsets of \(S\).
